statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 13% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, with Stress 52% elevated and Confidence 88% high.
recommendation: Conditions are described as low tail risk on a contained, mildly firm Globex tape holding inside a 71-point overnight band, set against an unresolved Middle East energy backdrop and a September policy debate priced near even odds. The single mapped danger window is the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September through 14:30Z, covering the release and the first hour of U.S. cash trade.
headline: NQ 29,549.50 drifts to the top of a 71-point Globex band ahead of the 12:30Z August employment report
body: The Globex session remains contained and only mildly firm. NQ traded 29,549.50 at 02:15Z, up 24.25 points or 0.08%, inside a 71-point 29,482.00-29,553.25 band since the reopen on roughly 16,500 contracts against 556,000 in the prior full session. The contract sits near the top of that band, but a 0.24% overnight range on minimal volume is a slow drift rather than the persistent no-retracement structure Tail measures, which is why Tail rises only one point to 13% and the dominant mode stays normal. E-mini S&P 500 futures corroborate the picture at 7,756.75, up 0.03% inside a 0.12% band. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,482.32, up 1.16%, within a 29,160.96-29,538.76 range, finishing roughly 56 points below its session high rather than pinned to it, and Reuters reported the S&P 500 up 1.06% at 7,747.71 and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.40% at 26,584.06. Thursday's driver was policy repricing rather than growth: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to let key rates stand should incoming data confirm easing price pressures, and CME FedWatch odds of a September quarter-point hike fell from 63.2% to 50.4%. The 2-year stood at 4.39% and the 10-year at 4.79% on the latest published H.15 column for 2 September, and VIX settled at 14.32, down 5.79%. Cross-asset alignment is incomplete rather than one-directional: seven of eight megacaps rose in the prior session while Broadcom fell after a narrow beat and softer fourth-quarter revenue guidance. The unresolved element is energy and geopolitics. Kuwait's armed forces said they intercepted Iranian missiles and drones on Thursday, Brent traded above $96 after briefly breaking $97 and WTI near $91.90, leaving crude up roughly 9% on the week, while Strait of Hormuz transit reached a wartime record of about 17 million barrels on Monday under U.S. military protection against a pre-war baseline near 20 million. That combination holds Stress at 52% without producing the persistent one-way path Tail measures. The dominant scheduled uncertainty is the August employment report at 12:30Z, where consensus sits near a 42,000 to 55,000 gain against a prior print of -23,000 and the unemployment rate is expected unchanged at 4.1%. That dispersion is mapped to Stress and Confidence, not to Tail, and the danger window covers 12:30Z through 14:30Z.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published state was green in 20 of the 24 assessed hours, and every hour carries a published assessment. Tail held between 12% and 15% from the Asian session through the European morning and into the early U.S. afternoon while Stress drifted from the mid 50s down to the low 50s. The state moved to yellow at 15:00Z and 16:00Z with Tail at 21% and 20% as the index held near its session extreme after the Waller remarks and the ISM services beat, returned to green at 17:00Z during consolidation, went yellow once more at 18:00Z on a fresh session high, then back to green from 19:00Z after that high was retraced and the index settled below it. Tail eased to 12% by 23:00Z and held there through the overnight reopen before this hour's one-point uptick.
outlookSummary: The near path keeps Tail in the low band while Globex trades inside a 71-point band on thin volume and the cash session has already settled 56 points below its high, holding 13% through the remaining Asian hours as participation stays minimal. Risk rebuilds gradually across European hours into the August employment report at 12:30Z, which anchors the mapped danger window through 14:30Z and covers both the release and the first hour of U.S. cash trade. Tail is deliberately capped at the top of the watch band across 12:00Z through 15:00Z because forecast dispersion and event magnitude raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than establishing a no-retracement price path; a higher score would require observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks, which cannot exist before the auction runs. Beyond 15:00Z the projection assumes orderly price discovery and decay back into the low band, with a modest late-session tick for Friday weekend-risk positioning while Middle East escalation stays unresolved. The final five hours fall inside the CME weekly halt from 21:00Z, where no price path can develop and Confidence is reduced accordingly.
